title: Sovereign Citizens: free speech or domestic terrorism?
summary: FBI podcast on domestic terrorism, the 2010 West Memphis police killings by sovereign citizens, and paper terrorism.

assertions.quote: they are willing to kill and be kill for these beliefs
we call it paper terrorism where their focus is mainly putting liens on officers or on judges
the officer has a right to give you a traffic ticket
the father and son had been traveling across the United States teaching these sovereign citizen classes
it's your First Amendment right to be a sovereign citizen if you want to

verdicts.note: In the US belief and speech are protected; investigation needs a crime, and the FBI requires force or violence for domestic terrorism.

The Ninth Circuit says sovereign-citizen beliefs are not a sign of incompetence and that a defendant may argue unorthodox theories 'to the bitter end'; he was convicted for filing false liens, not for the beliefs.
The FBI definition quoted in the review says mere advocacy or philosophic embrace of these positions may be constitutionally protected, with extremism defined by unlawful acts.
